commit.message:
Allow annotating relative diagnostic paths

Some config objects like list and actions now always contain a `config`
block for nont-meta-attributes. Since the `config` block is the only
value sent to the provider, diagnostics from the provider will always be
returned relative to this block, so we need to prefix the stored path
with the config block name.

Call InConfigBody with entire action block

The grpc provider adapters will now correctly annotate diagnostics
relative to the outermost config block, so non-attribute errors don't
always just point to the `config` block name.

Create a better "with" string for actions, indicating both the action
address, and the caller address.

render cycle errors vertically

Large configs often return cycle errors which are very long, and
difficult to parse on a single line. Render cycles vertically, visually
separating each node.

Reverse the cycle order, so the dependencies are read in the order of
references as opposed to traversal order.

Pick a single starting node for output consistency.

Cleanup after 1.16.0-alpha20260617 release (#38738)

commit.message:
policy: resolve plugin entitlement from the backend

The policy plugin needs the host, token, and organization of the calling
HCP Terraform org to verify policy-enforcement entitlement at Setup time.
Previously the plugin scraped this itself, which missed most credential
sources. Now core resolves the triple and passes it on the Setup RPC.

The cloud and remote backends resolve the host/token/org while configuring,
so they expose it through a new EntitlementProvider interface. Init, plan,
and apply all read it from the configured backend: init sets up the policy
client after the backend is initialized so it can use the same source.

Adds an Entitlement message to PolicySetupRequest and regenerates the proto
stubs.

commit.message:
use GraphNodeConfigAction

Bring back GraphNodeConfigAction into use, so we can get the last
hardcoded type out of the reference transformer to ensure we're handling
nodes by behavior and not by name.

The reference transformer still carried some cruft to deal with the fact
that nodes were sloppy about their references. Finishing the cleanup of
reference handling means we don't need special exceptions for what can
be a referencer.

The only remaining exception are action config nodes, which must remain
in place because the config structure allowed them to create cycles and
will forever need special handling.

remove hasBeforeActions since they no longer require special behavior in
the graph, so there's no need to guard them.

remove extra method callRange method params

better variable names

There is no need to run reference transformer for resource dynamic
expansion. The subgraph is entirely separate from the full graph, and
individual instance nodes can't reference each other.

policy: Add resource and module policy evaluation support to stacks (#38748)

As policy evaluation is implemented in the module runtime, this change is mostly focused on adding tests to stacks around policy evaluation and publishing those policy results from the module runtime as a new event during PlanStackChanges and ApplyStackChanges. Policies are not evaluated during refresh or destroy plans in the module runtime, so that logic is reflected in stacks as well.

Notably this change does not add support for provider policy evaluation because providers are configured outside of the module runtime in stacks. A follow-up change will introduce this support to the stacks runtime

fix: Only throw errors if the lock files supplied via CLI flags don't exist; it's valid to not have a dep lock file in the working directory.

It would be unusual for someone to perform a migration with no lock file already present, but we need to be prepared for unusual use cases/workflows. The command would download both providers in this scenario but only persist the destination provider in a new lock file.
